classification.difficultyReason: Locate the possible right angle and use symbolic perpendicular gradients to determine an exact positive coordinate.

content.prompt: Find the value of $k>0$ if the triangle shown below has a right angle.

spec.description: Unfilled triangle with base on the x-axis from −2 to 3 and apex on the positive y-axis labelled k. Preserve the absence of a right-angle marker, numeric y-ticks and origin label.
spec.mathematics: Vertices are (-2,0), (3,0) and (0,k), with k>0. The display height is schematic and does not specify a numerical value of k.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied labels appear. No right-angle location or value of k is revealed.

answer.short:
$k=\sqrt{6}$.

The two sloping sides are perpendicular, so their gradients have product $-1$.
answer.worked:
Neither base angle can be a right angle: a side perpendicular to the horizontal base would be vertical, but the apex has a different $x$-coordinate from both base vertices. Thus the two sloping sides are perpendicular.

Their gradients are $\frac{k}{2}$ and $-\frac{k}{3}$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{k}{2}\left(-\frac{k}{3}\right)&=-1\\-\frac{k^2}{6}&=-1\\k^2&=6\\k&=\sqrt{6},\qquad k>0.\end{align*}$$
